subject: CloudQuotient — commit pricing, overage handling, and invoice export
messages:
From: Peter Holt <peter.holt@cloudquotient.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, procurement@cloudquotient.com
Date: Mon, 08 Jun 2026 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Pricing clarification and invoice export request

Hi Neha,

Thanks for the call earlier — CloudQuotient is very interested in a committed usage arrangement for Redwood's hosted API. Before we move to a PO, procurement needs two things from us:

1) A clear breakdown of commit tiers and the per-token effective price at each tier (including how embeddings are priced relative to text generation).
2) A sample invoice (line items) or CSV export that shows the per-request/token fields so our billing team can map to our internal chargeback system.

Two specific questions: if we commit, how are overages billed? Do they fall to the public rate, or do you apply the next tier price? And can we get programmatic access to a usage export that includes prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, and route/model metadata?

Procurement contact: procurement@cloudquotient.com.

Can you send a concise proposal and sample export by EOD Wednesday? We want to review with finance.

Best,
Peter
Head of Platform Ops
CloudQuotient

--

(Attachment: none in this message)
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Peter Holt <peter.holt@cloudquotient.com>
Cc: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 08 Jun 2026 17:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing clarification and invoice export request

Hi Peter — thanks for the clear list. Putting everything below so procurement has what it needs. I've attached a compact pricing grid and a synthetic usage CSV to show the export format.

High level commit options (hosted, per-token billing):
- Pay-as-you-go (no commit): list price.
- Small commit (1M tokens/month minimum): 10% off list for all tokens up to commit.
- Mid commit (10M tokens/month): 18% off list for tokens up to 10M.
- Large commit (50M+ tokens/month): 28% off list for tokens up to 50M.

Notes on semantics:
- Discounts apply to tokens consumed up to the committed units at the discounted effective unit price.
- Overages are billed at the public list price by default. We can also offer an overage-tier (e.g., overage capped at the next lower discount) as a negotiated term for multiyear deals; we typically leave that for legal/sales to finalize.

Embeddings vs text: embeddings consume "embedding units" (per 1k vectors) and are priced separately in the grid; both prompt/completion tokens and embeddings appear in the usage export schema.

Export & line-item details:
- We can turn on a usage export for your billing contact; the CSV includes: timestamp, request_id, route (e.g., /v1/chat/completions), model, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, embedding_units, cost_cents, and request_tags.
- Example file: usage_sample.csv (attached).
- Example line-item mapping (how we render invoice rows): one row per API call by default; we also offer rolled-up invoice views that show daily aggregates per route/model.

Next steps we propose:
1) I’ll share a short SOW/quote with the banded pricing above (attached: commit_pricing_grid.xlsx).
2) If acceptable, we’ll issue a quote for signature and enable the usage-export webhook/CSV for procurement to pull a 90-day sample.
3) We’ll loop legal for any overage carryover or true-up terms.

If you want, I can surface a recommended default (for fast approval): mid commit (10M/month) with a 12-month term and a 30% upfront credit against the first invoice to smooth month-one usage.

Let me know if you want me to reduce the options to a single recommended plan for finance.

Cheers,
Neha Kapoor
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachments: commit_pricing_grid.xlsx, usage_sample.csv
From: Peter Holt <peter.holt@cloudquotient.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@cloudquotient.com
Date: Tue, 09 Jun 2026 09:11:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing clarification and invoice export request

Neha — thanks for the quick turnaround and the attachments. A couple follow-ups from our finance team after looking at the sample CSV:

- Can you confirm whether "cost_cents" in your sample is pre-discount or post-discount? Finance needs to reconcile the invoice entries back to committed unit pricing.
- For rollups: instead of one row per API call (which will be millions of rows), we prefer daily aggregates per route/model with token columns split. Can you provide a sample aggregate export?
- Overages: CloudQuotient wants a predictable overage rule. Public list price is acceptable if there's a rollback/true-up quarterly (i.e., if we exceed commit, we pay public price but can negotiate a quarterly true-up to migrate to the next band at the effective rate). Would Redwood be open to that as a negotiated clause?

If you can answer these, we can route to procurement and legal.

Thanks,
Peter

On Mon, Jun 8, 2026 at 5:08 PM Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Hi Peter — thanks for the clear list...
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Peter Holt <peter.holt@cloudquotient.com>
Cc: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, procurement@cloudquotient.com
Date: Tue, 09 Jun 2026 11:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing clarification and invoice export request

Hi Peter — answers inline below and a proposal for a predictable overage path.

- cost_cents in sample CSV: currently shows pre-discounted cost (list-derived cost). The exported CSV includes both list_cost_cents and post_discount_cost_cents columns when a commit is active. We'll enable post_discount_cost_cents for your billing team so your reconciliation is straightforward.

- Aggregates: we can produce a daily-aggregated export with the following columns: date, route, model, prompt_tokens_total, completion_tokens_total, embedding_units_total, list_cost_cents, post_discount_cost_cents. I attached line_item_mapping.txt as a quick reference for how we map request fields -> invoice line items.

- Overage handling proposal (negotiable):
  Option A (default): overages billed at public list price; quarterly true-up to evaluate moving to the next band if sustained.
  Option B (negotiated): overage cap at the next discount band for the first 2 quarters after commit, then revert to list price; requires CFO sign-off.

To keep things moving, I'm looping in Sean (Finance) and Grace (Legal) to confirm whether Option B requires an internal approval for a 25–28% cap on overage pricing.

If that works, I can prepare a one-page quote that reflects Option B with a 25% overage cap for the first 90 days, then automatic evaluation.

Thanks — I’ll stand by for procurement to confirm which option they prefer.

Best,
Neha

Attachments: line_item_mapping.txt
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Peter Holt <peter.holt@cloudquotient.com>
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing clarification and invoice export request

Neha / Peter — quick note from finance: we can enable Option B for a trial period but need to cap the deepest discount exposure. Please amend the large-commit discount ceiling to 25% (instead of 28%) for approval by our CFO. Also, any overage cap should be time-limited and include a quarterly true-up clause.

Once the quote reflects 25% max discount and the 90-day overage cap, finance will greenlight.

- Sean
VP, Finance
Redwood Inference

Neha / Sean — thanks, that all makes sense. CloudQuotient is happy to proceed with:

- Mid commit: 10M tokens/month, 18% discount on committed units.
- Overage guard: 90-day capped overage at 25% discount (per Sean's note), quarterly true-up to move to the appropriate tier if sustained.
- Redwood to enable a daily-aggregated usage export with both list_cost_cents and post_discount_cost_cents for procurement to pull.

Please send the one-page quote and a sample of the aggregated export (CSV) so procurement can attach to the PO. Also include the billing contact and a billing email to receive the signed quote.

If you can have the quote over by Friday EOD that would be great.

Appreciate the responsiveness — looking forward to partnering.
